summary: 90-foot Aermotor MC-39 tower in Douglas County, WA, believed moved from a reservation and now hosting communications gear; registered 2026, no build date found.

events.note: Register believes the tower was previously used on an Indian reservation for fire detection before reaching its present site; move date and origin not recorded
Believed to have stood at the present site since at least the mid-1980s (register's belief, not a dated record)

evidence.supports: 90-foot Aermotor MC-39 tower; little known of its history
evidence.quote: Not much is known about the history of this 90-foot Aermotor MC-39 tower.

evidence.supports: Believed previous use on a reservation for fire detection; now hosts communications equipment
evidence.quote: It is believed to have previously been used on an Indian reservation for fire detection work, but at its current location, it hosts communications equipment.

evidence.supports: Believed at the present site since at least the mid-1980s
evidence.quote: It is believed to have been at this current site since at least the mid-1980s.

evidence.supports: Aermotor made several lookout models, including the MC-39
evidence.quote: including the LS-50, LS-40 and MC-39

evidence.supports: A different 130-foot lookout west of Rocky Butte is not in the historic listings
evidence.quote: The North Douglas County Lookout west of Rocky Butte, which is not in the historic tower listings, but standing proud on a 130-foot tower.

evidence.supports: Washington list marks the Rocky Butte tower as standing under NHLR US 1815
evidence.quote: Douglas 48.05433 -119.72301 Tower Standing NHLR US 1815, WA 94

corrections.current: None relocated (Moved to Rocky Butte from a site not recorded.)
corrections.proposed: relocated, year unknown, from a site not recorded
corrections.why: The register gives no move date and only believes the tower was used elsewhere; 'None relocated' contradicts the note that follows it.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 130-foot lookout west of Rocky Butte in a Wenatchee World photo caption is a different structure. The 90-foot figure belongs to the Rocky Butte tower per the register.

sources.title: The Aermotor Company: From Windmills to Forest Lookout Towers
Badger Mountain Lookout Tower: Fire protection and history in NCW

notes_for_editor: Only the register page is specific to this tower; the reservation origin is the register's belief, not a documented fact. The HistoryLink essay on Washington lookouts and the Aermotor PDF were read; only the Aermotor PDF gave model context. Search hits for 'Rocky Butte' lookouts in California and Oregon are unrelated. The Wenatchee World caption (photo credit Earl Cater, who also nominated this tower) describes a 130-foot North Douglas County Lookout west of Rocky Butte, which may be the source of confusion for the record. The brief's events line 'None relocated (Moved to Rocky Butte from a site not recorded.)' is malformed; see corrections. The brief lists the agency as Unknown, and the register does not name one, so no agency is recorded. No access information was found.
